newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia-Thai authority confirms Bulan gas find.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia-Thai authority confirms Bulan gas find.

text.p: The Malaysia-Thailand Joint Authority (MTJA) said its contractors have made a new gas find in a field off Songkhla, southern Thailand, and off Kota Bharu, northeast Malaysia.
The tests on Well Bulan-2 yielded a combined gas flow rate of 30 million standard cubic feet per day, and 185 barrels per day of condensate, the MTJA, said in a statement on Thursday.
The MTJA develops overlapping gas and oil assets between Malaysia and Thailand.
It said the well -- located 260 km east of Songkhla and 140 km northeast of Kota Bharu -- is about four km off Well Bulan-1, another proven gas well, the statement said.
Well Bulan-2 was spudded on September 17 and drilled to 9,160 feet, the statement said, adding that two drill stem tests were conducted over the depth intervals' range of 3,750 to 8,402 feet.
The operators of the well -- Carigali-Triton Operating Co Sdn Bhd, Petronas Carigali Sdn Bhd and Triton Oil Co of Thailand -- said it was in the process of plugging and abandoning the well.
